input.question: How was German culture effected by the years between the end of WWII and reunification?
input.ground_truth: I'm not a historian, but a German. So in fact there were two countries, DDR and BRD, or East Germany and West Germany. But in both countries the people were mostly german and spoke german. So there was no big cultural difference, except maybe food. Regarding patriotism: There was just a minority of people who were against a unification of the DDR and the BRD. The people were smart enough to see that the communist part of the world was crumbling and they wanted to be free. After the unification background checks of the administrative elite were executed. So you didn't really have supporters of the old regime in important positions anymore. I don't know if this answers your questions.

For many years, the people in the two houses grew up a little differently. The kids in the first house learned to listen to different music, eat different foods, and play different games. The kids in the other house learned different songs and played with different toys because the grown-ups in charge were different and told them to do things a certain way.

When the two houses finally got back together (reunification), the kids and grown-ups had to learn from each other. Some people were excited to share their toys and games, but some were a little sad or confused because things changed so fast. They had to learn new ways of doing things and sometimes it was hard to agree on what to do together.

So, German culture changed a lot during those years because the country was split and then came back together, and everyone had to learn to play nicely and share again.
